scenes.tts: A receptor activates Ras without ever touching it. How does the message cross the gap? Watch the blue receptor and purple Ras. Both sit at the membrane, but nothing yet connects them.
scenes.caption: A receptor activates Ras without ever touching it. How does the message cross the gap? Watch the blue receptor and purple Ras. Both sit at the membrane, but nothing yet connects them.
scenes.visual: COLOR MAP for both films: receptor or input blue; binding organizer green; enzyme orange; output switch purple; phosphate gold; membrane and inactive labels light gray. Fill the frame with a gray membrane. A blue receptor activates on the left. Purple Ras drifts in the membrane at right. A dotted question mark sits between them; keep both proteins drifting freely. Label all blocks 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: A receptor activates Ras without ever touching it. How does the message cross the gap? Watch the blue receptor and purple Ras. Both sit at the membrane, but nothing yet connects them.

scenes.visual: Transform the dotted question path into the title 'How a Receptor Reaches Ras'. Keep the membrane, receptor and Ras visible behind it. Fade the title before the next scene.

scenes.tts: A growth factor makes the receptor add phosphate marks to its tail. Each gold mark is a possible docking site. Yet a phosphate cannot activate Ras by itself.
scenes.caption: A growth factor makes the receptor add phosphate marks to its tail. Each gold mark is a possible docking site. Yet a phosphate cannot activate Ras by itself.
scenes.visual: A blue growth-factor block lands outside the receptor. The receptor tails move together, then gold phosphate badges appear sequentially. One badge pulses while a dashed arrow toward Ras stops halfway. An orange enzyme silhouette waits beyond the gap.
scenes.narration: A growth factor makes the receptor add phosphate marks to its tail. Each gold mark is a possible docking site. Yet a phosphate cannot activate Ras by itself.

scenes.tts: The receptor and Ras are separate proteins, each free to drift in the membrane. The missing part must bind the receptor without consuming its phosphate. It must also carry something that can act on Ras.
scenes.caption: The receptor and Ras are separate proteins, each free to drift in the membrane. The missing part must bind the receptor without consuming its phosphate. It must also carry something that can act on Ras.
scenes.visual: Blue receptor and purple Ras both drift slowly on the gray membrane; do not hold them fixed or draw a span between them. An empty green outline rises from the cytoplasm: one end reaches the gold phosphate, while the orange enzyme silhouette waits below, not yet attached. Do not name or label the outline.
scenes.narration: The receptor and Ras are separate proteins, each free to drift in the membrane. The missing part must bind the receptor without consuming its phosphate. It must also carry something that can act on Ras.

scenes.tts: The reader is Grb2, a green adaptor with no enzyme activity. Its central S H 2 domain is a cup for phosphotyrosine. Its S H 3 domains are paired grips. Those grips already hold the orange exchange factor Sos.
scenes.caption: The reader is Grb2, a green adaptor with no enzyme activity. Its central SH2 domain is a cup for phosphotyrosine. Its SH3 domains are paired grips. Those grips already hold the orange exchange factor Sos.
scenes.visual: Fill the empty green outline below the receptor: it becomes a large green Grb2 cartoon with a central cup labelled 'SH2' and two side grips labelled 'SH3'. Do not draw molecular structure. The waiting orange Sos block slides into both grips. A small 'no enzyme activity' tag settles beneath Grb2.
scenes.narration: The reader is Grb2, a green adaptor with no enzyme activity. Its central SH2 domain is a cup for phosphotyrosine. Its SH3 domains are paired grips. Those grips already hold the orange exchange factor Sos.

scenes.tts: Which part should face the phosphorylated receptor: the S H 2 cup or an S H 3 grip? Keep your choice in mind while the two shapes move toward the gold phosphate.
scenes.caption: Which part should face the phosphorylated receptor: the SH2 cup or an SH3 grip? Keep your choice in mind while the two shapes move toward the gold phosphate.
scenes.visual: Hold the receptor tail large at left. Place the green SH2 cup and one SH3 grip beside it at equal distance. Both rock toward the gold phosphate, then stop. Keep the question on screen without revealing an answer.
scenes.narration: Which part should face the phosphorylated receptor: the SH2 cup or an SH3 grip? Keep your choice in mind while the two shapes move toward the gold phosphate.

scenes.visual: Maintain the question and the two moving choices. Let the gold phosphate pulse slowly and the two shapes hover. Reveal nothing during the thinking pause.

scenes.tts: The S H 2 cup closes around the receptor phosphotyrosine. The S H 3 grips keep holding Sos. The complete Grb2 and Sos unit moves to the receptor tail. The adaptor has connected a marked receptor to an enzyme.
scenes.caption: The SH2 cup closes around the receptor phosphotyrosine. The SH3 grips keep holding Sos. The complete Grb2 and Sos unit moves to the receptor tail. The adaptor has connected a marked receptor to an enzyme.
scenes.visual: The SH3 choice slides away. The SH2 cup closes visibly around the gold badge. Rebuild the full green Grb2 with orange Sos in the same position. Draw a bright path from blue receptor through green Grb2 to orange Sos; Ras drifts nearby, not yet touched.
scenes.narration: The SH2 cup closes around the receptor phosphotyrosine. The SH3 grips keep holding Sos. The complete Grb2 and Sos unit moves to the receptor tail. The adaptor has connected a marked receptor to an enzyme.

scenes.tts: Membrane-bound Ras now meets the recruited Sos. Sos is a guanine-nucleotide exchange factor. It releases G D P from Ras, allowing G T P to bind. Purple Ras changes from off to on. Grb2 never catalyzes that exchange.
scenes.caption: Membrane-bound Ras now meets the recruited Sos. Sos is a guanine-nucleotide exchange factor. It releases GDP from Ras, allowing GTP to bind. Purple Ras changes from off to on. Grb2 never catalyzes that exchange.
scenes.visual: Purple Ras diffuses along the membrane into the region around the receptor, where orange Sos now sits. A gray 'GDP' tag leaves Ras and a bright 'GTP' tag replaces it; show labels only, with no molecular structures. Ras brightens and its 'OFF' label transforms to 'ON'. The green Grb2 block remains unchanged.
scenes.narration: Membrane-bound Ras now meets the recruited Sos. Sos is a guanine-nucleotide exchange factor. It releases GDP from Ras, allowing GTP to bind. Purple Ras changes from off to on. Grb2 never catalyzes that exchange.

scenes.tts: Recruitment changes location, not chemical identity. Sos was already attached to Grb2 in the cytoplasm. After the S H 2 cup docks, the same Sos sits at the membrane, where it can meet Ras. Positioning has become a decisive signaling step.
scenes.caption: Recruitment changes location, not chemical identity. Sos was already attached to Grb2 in the cytoplasm. After the SH2 cup docks, the same Sos sits at the membrane, where it can meet Ras. Positioning has become a decisive signaling step.
scenes.visual: Split the frame into before and after states without cutting worlds. On the left, green Grb2 holds orange Sos in cytoplasm. Slide that unchanged pair to the receptor on the right. A location pin moves with Sos and settles at the membrane; mobile Ras drifts nearby.
scenes.narration: Recruitment changes location, not chemical identity. Sos was already attached to Grb2 in the cytoplasm. After the SH2 cup docks, the same Sos sits at the membrane, where it can meet Ras. Positioning has become a decisive signaling step.

scenes.tts: Sos also has another Ras-binding site, away from the exchange site. Ras with G T P can bind there and speed Sos. One activated Ras can therefore help Sos activate more, once recruitment starts.
scenes.caption: Sos also has another Ras-binding site, away from the exchange site. Ras with GTP can bind there and speed Sos. One activated Ras can therefore help Sos activate more, once recruitment starts.
scenes.visual: Add a second simple notch to the orange Sos block, clearly separate from the exchange notch. One bright purple Ras-GTP block docks there. Animate the exchange tags on a neighboring Ras moving faster; label the acceleration arrow 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: Sos also has another Ras-binding site, away from the exchange site. Ras with GTP can bind there and speed Sos. One activated Ras can therefore help Sos activate more, once recruitment starts.

scenes.tts: Now follow the route once. The receptor recruits Grb2. Grb2 brings Sos to the membrane, where Ras sits. Sos performs the exchange that activates Ras. Binding controls the encounter, while Sos performs the chemical work.
scenes.caption: Now follow the route once. The receptor recruits Grb2. Grb2 brings Sos to the membrane, where Ras sits. Sos performs the exchange that activates Ras. Binding controls the encounter, while Sos performs the chemical work.
scenes.visual: Zoom out to the full membrane world. Illuminate the blue receptor, green Grb2, orange Sos and purple Ras in sequence. A moving pulse travels along their connections. Keep a separate catalytic flash only between Sos and Ras.
scenes.narration: Now follow the route once. The receptor recruits Grb2. Grb2 brings Sos to the membrane, where Ras sits. Sos performs the exchange that activates Ras. Binding controls the encounter, while Sos performs the chemical work.

scenes.tts: The missing link from the opening is filled, but the receptor still never touches Ras. The adaptor changes who meets whom and where. It lets the right enzyme reach its target without the adaptor being an enzyme itself.
scenes.caption: The missing link from the opening is filled, but the receptor still never touches Ras. The adaptor changes who meets whom and where. It lets the right enzyme reach its target without the adaptor being an enzyme itself.
scenes.visual: Restore the opening wide view. Show the receptor, green adaptor and orange Sos as one compact cluster at the membrane, with purple Ras ON beside Sos after drifting in. Do not draw a bridge across a gap. Remove every label except 'adaptor', 'enzyme' and 'Ras ON' as the route pulses.
scenes.narration: The missing link from the opening is filled, but the receptor still never touches Ras. The adaptor changes who meets whom and where. It lets the right enzyme reach its target without the adaptor being an enzyme itself.

scenes.visual: Show one line only, centered and large: 'Adaptors route signals by linking partners, not by catalyzing reactions.' No title, logo, subtitle, URL or smaller line. Let a faint green connection grow beneath the sentence without adding text.
